newsitem.title: USA: GE, French firm wins $1.1 billion engine order.
newsitem.headline: GE, French firm wins $1.1 billion engine order.

text.p: General Electric Co. and the French firm SNECMA are being awarded a $1.1 billion U.S. defence contract for 267 engines for KC-135 tanker planes and RC-135 reconnaissance planes, the Air Force said on Tuesday.
The firms have been jointly producing engines for the big U.S. military jets for more than a decade and the new engines are part of an upgrade programme, the Air Force said.
The companies produce the CFM-56 engines as a joint firm called CFM International of Cincinnati, Ohio.
The work, 51 percent by General Electric and 49 percent by SNECMA, on the contract is expected to be completed by April of 2002.
The Air Force said that CFM International was the only firm which received a solicitation for the contract and the only firm which submitted a bid. Negotiations were completed last September.
